strings.title: Give and Take with Decimals
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: When one number is close to a friendly number, give it what it needs from the other number. The total stays the same, with whole numbers or decimals.
strings.keywords: give and take, friendly number, total stays the same, decimals, thousandths
watchFor: Making the friendly number but not taking from the other: ask "Where did the extra come from?"
Giving the wrong amount with decimals (4.98 + 3.37 = 5 + 3.35 + ...): ask "How much does 4.98 need to make 5?"
Lining up 6.995 + 2.15 wrong: ask "About how much should it be?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How much did each friendly number need?" Land: find what the number needs (4.98 needs 0.02), move it from the other number, then add. The total doesn't change.

problems.notes: Look for: give 2: 400 + 243. Ask: "What does 398 need?" Model: givetake 398 + 245 = 400 + 243
Look for: give 3: 3000 + 1465. Ask: "Same idea, bigger numbers?" Model: givetake 2997 + 1468 = 3000 + 1465

responses.tip: Gave 3 but didn't take it. Ask: where did the 3 come from?

problems.notes: Look for: give 0.02: 5 + 3.35. Ask: "What does 4.98 need?" Word choice: "give and take". Model: givetake 4.98 + 3.37 = 5 + 3.35
Look for: give 0.005: 7 + 2.145. Ask: "How far is 6.995 from 7?" Model: givetake 6.995 + 2.15 = 7 + 2.145

responses.tip: Gave 0.05, not 0.005. Ask: how far is 6.995 from 7?

problems.notes: Look for: 1 + 0.447. Ask: "Is the answer more or less than 1.45?" Model: givetake 0.997 + 0.45 = 1 + 0.447
Look for: 20 + 7.84. Ask: "How is this like money?" Model: givetake 19.99 + 7.85 = 20 + 7.84
Look for: 0.75 + 0.25 = 1 first. Ask: "Which two go together?" Model: text 0.75 + 0.25 = 1 ; 1 + 2.99 = 3.99

strings.title: Estimate, Then Calculate
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Estimate with friendly numbers first, so you know about how big the answer should be. Then calculate, and check it's close to the estimate.
strings.keywords: estimate, about, friendly numbers, benchmark, check, reasonable
watchFor: Skipping the estimate: ask "About how much should it be?"
An answer far from the estimate (3.98 + 5.1 = 4.49): ask "Your estimate was 9. Is 4.49 close?"
Estimating fractions badly (4/5 + 7/10 is about 11/15): ask "Is each fraction close to 0, 1/2 or 1?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did the estimate help?" Land: round to friendly numbers (whole numbers, halves) to get about how big the answer is. If the calculation is far off, check it.

problems.notes: Look for: about 4 + 5 = 9, then 4 + 5.1 − 0.02. Ask: "About how much?" Model: estimate 3.98 + 5.1

responses.tip: Lined up digits from the right. Ask: your estimate was 9. Is 4.49 close?

problems.notes: Look for: about 12 − 8 = 4. Then slide: 12.08 − 8. Ask: "What's your estimate?" Model: estimate 12.04 - 7.96
Look for: both close to 1, so a bit less than 2. Exactly 8/10 + 7/10 = 15/10. Ask: "Close to 0, 1/2 or 1?" Model: numberline 4/5 +1/5 +1/2

responses.tip: Ask: both fractions are near 1. Can the total be less than 1?

problems.notes: Look for: about 3 + 1 = 4. 1/8 makes 3, then 1 1/8. Ask: "Will it be more or less than 4?" Model: numberline 2 7/8 +1/8 +1 +1/8
Look for: about 10 − 5 = 5. Then 9.875 − 5 + 0.1. Ask: "Bigger or smaller than 5?" Model: numberline 9.875 -5 +0.1

responses.tip: Ask: did you take away all of 4.9?

problems.notes: Look for: about 3 − 2 = 1, a bit more. 1/6 to 2, then 1 1/3: 1 3/6. Ask: "Is your answer close to the estimate?" Model: numberline 1 5/6 >2 >3 1/3
Look for: 0.49 + 0.51 = 1, plus almost 1. Ask: "What's the estimate?" Model: text 0.49 + 0.51 = 1 ; 1 + 0.999 = 1.999

strings.title: Whole Numbers and Decimals: Choose a Strategy
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Look at the numbers before you start. Close together? Count up. Small amount to take? Take it away. Near a friendly number? Use it and adjust. Partners? Put them together.
strings.keywords: choose, count up, take away, friendly number, partners, near double
watchFor: Using the algorithm for 7002 − 6995: ask "Are these close together?"
Counting up from 15 to 7002: ask "Is 15 a small amount to take away?"
Missing partners like 25.5 + 24.5: ask "What do 0.5 and 0.5 make?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "What did you look for before choosing?" Land: how close the numbers are, whether one is near a friendly number, and whether there are partners. The numbers tell you the strategy.

problems.notes: Look for: count up 5 to 7000, then 2. Ask: "Close together?" Model: numberline 6995 >7000 >7002
Look for: back 2 to 7000, back 13. Ask: "Why not count up this time?" Model: numberline 7002 -2 -13

responses.tip: Ask: if you take 2 you're at 7000. How much more to take?

problems.notes: Look for: 5 + 5 − 0.02. Ask: "What's 4.99 close to?" Model: text 4.99 + 4.99 = 5 + 5 - 0.02 = 9.98

responses.tip: Took back only once. Ask: how short is each number?

problems.notes: Look for: back 0.6 to 3, back 0.15. Or 3.6 − 1 + 0.25. Ask: "Which way?" Model: numberline 3.6 -1 +0.25
Look for: 0.5 + 0.5 = 1, so 49 + 1. Ask: "Partners?" Model: split 25.5 + 24.5
Look for: count up 3, 60, 300; or 999 − 636. Ask: "How would you avoid the zeros?" Model: slide 1000 - 637 = 999 - 636
Look for: 0.003 to 6, then 0.004. Ask: "How far apart are they?" Model: numberline 5.997 >6 >6.004

strings.title: Add It, Then Undo It
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Each subtraction here undoes the addition before it, with whole numbers, decimals and fractions. If a + b = c, then c − b = a.
strings.keywords: inverse, undo, add, subtract, check, related facts
watchFor: Recalculating every subtraction from scratch: ask "Did the problem before help?"
Undoing with the wrong number: ask "Which number are we taking away? What was it added to?"
Not checking: ask "How could you check that subtraction by adding?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why didn't we have to work out the subtractions?" Land: addition and subtraction undo each other. If 1998 + 2005 = 4003, then 4003 − 1998 = 2005. Use this to check any subtraction.

problems.notes: Look for: give 2: 2000 + 2003. Ask: "What's 1998 close to?" Model: givetake 1998 + 2005 = 2000 + 2003
Look for: it undoes the last one. Ask: "Do you need to calculate?" Word choice: "undo". Model: numberline 1998 >2000 >4003
Look for: 2.75 + 0.25 = 3, then 1.25. Ask: "Partners?" Model: numberline 2.75 +0.25 +1.25
Look for: undo. Ask: "Which addition helps?" Model: numberline 2.75 >3 >4.25
Look for: 5/10 + 4/10. Ask: "What common piece?" Model: numberline 0 +1/2 +2/5

responses.tip: Added tops and bottoms. Ask: is 3/7 more than 1/2?

problems.notes: Look for: undo the last one. Ask: "Do you need a common denominator now?" Model: numberline 1/2 >9/10
Look for: 2/5 = 0.4, so 6.4 − 2.4. Ask: "What's 2/5 as a decimal?" Model: numberline 2.4 >6.4
